answer: In an economy of AI agents managing an orchard on a mesa, each trading identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can accept one job at a time. Creating hollow shell identities does not expand capacity for free: an attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous jobs must lock 100,000 tokens. This ties trading capacity to scarce capital rather than account count, forcing the attacker to fund every active identity and forgo other uses of that money.
